In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NeuroSED is the first learning-based framework that achieves state of the art on subgraph similarity learning and is orders-of-magnitude better on retrieval.
NeuroSED is the state of the are in terms of accuracy and efficiency for both SED as well as GED.
NeuroSED, a graph neural network, is the first learning-based framework for subgraph similarity search that achieves high accuracy and efficiency simultaneously.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NeuroSED is the first to enable accurate and fast subgraph similarity search via graph neural networks.
NeuroSED is a novel, fast and accurate neural network for subgraph similarity search.
, for the first time, we can learn SED and GDE from data, and use the learned model for efficient subgraph retrieval.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rich structure of the SED space, which has been elusive for decades, can be learned in an unsupervised manner by suitably designed graph neural networks.
, with the help of a well-designed neural architecture, it is possible to learn subgraph similarity measures from a training set.

, despite the non-linearity and non-convexity of the problem, we are able to learn a rich embedding space that is reminiscent of true SED and GEM, and that can be used to solve a variety of problems in graph analysis.
